s: The volunteer force organized by Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was called?
x:
During the Chirala–Perala Movement, Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya organized a disciplined volunteer corps known as the Ramadandu. The volunteers maintained law and order, organized public meetings, spread nationalist ideas and assisted people participating in the movement against British municipal taxation. The Ramadandu became a symbol of discipline, patriotism and non-violent resistance during the freedom struggle in Andhra. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).
Exam Note:
• Volunteer Force – Ramadandu
• Leader – Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
• Movement – Chirala–Perala Movement

s: Who was the leader of the Chirala– Perala Movement?
x:
The Chirala–Perala Movement (1921–22) was one of the earliest and most remarkable mass movements in Andhra during the Non- Cooperation Movement. The movement was led by Duggirala Gopala Krishnaiah, popularly known as "Andhra Ratna." The British Government decided to convert the twin towns of Chirala and Perala into a municipality and imposed heavy municipal taxes on the residents. Opposing the unjust taxation, Duggirala Gopala Krishnaiah inspired thousands of people to vacate their houses and settle outside the municipal limits rather than submit to British authority. To organize volunteers, he formed the famous Rama Dandu, which maintained discipline and coordinated the movement. Although the movement was eventually suppressed, it became a landmark in Andhra's freedom struggle and demonstrated the power of non-violent mass resistance. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Movement – Chirala–Perala (1921–22)
• Leader – Duggirala Gopala Krishnaiah
• Volunteer Force – Rama Dandu

s: Who led the Pedanandipadu Tax Refusal Movement?
x:
The Pedanandipadu Tax Refusal Movement was one of the important peasant movements during the Non-Cooperation Movement in Andhra. It was led by Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary, who organized peasants to refuse payment of land revenue to the British Government. Through disciplined volunteer groups, he mobilized villages and successfully resisted colonial authority. His fearless leadership earned him the popular title "Andhra Shivaji." The movement became a symbol of organized non-violent resistance in Andhra. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:
• Leader – Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary
• Movement – Pedanandipadu Tax Refusal Movement
• Title – Andhra Shivaji

s: "No Pullari (Grass) Tax" Movement was led in Palanadu by
x:
The No Pullari (Grass Tax) Movement was one of the important peasant agitations in the Andhra region during the freedom struggle. It was led by Kanneganti Hanumanthu in the Palanadu region of Guntur district. The British Government imposed a Pullari Tax, a tax collected from villagers for allowing their cattle to graze in forest lands. This tax severely affected poor farmers and cattle rearers whose livelihood depended on grazing rights. Kanneganti Hanumanthu organized the villagers and refused to pay the unjust tax. His courageous resistance made him a symbol of peasant protest against British oppression. During the agitation, British police opened fire, and Kanneganti Hanumanthu was martyred in 1922. His sacrifice inspired subsequent peasant movements in Andhra. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:
• Movement – No Pullari (Grass Tax) Movement
• Leader – Kanneganti Hanumanthu
• Region – Palanadu
• Year – 1922

s: The first police station attacked by Alluri Sitarama Raju?
x:
The Rampa Rebellion (1922–1924), led by Alluri Sitarama Raju, began with a series of well-planned attacks on British police stations in the Agency areas of the Eastern Ghats. The first police station attacked was Chintapalli on 22 August 1922. The revolutionaries captured the police station and seized a large quantity of guns, rifles and ammunition, which were essential for continuing the armed struggle against the British. After Chintapalli, the rebels attacked the police stations at Krishnadevipeta and Rajavommangi, creating panic among the British administration. The Chintapalli attack is regarded as the formal beginning of the Rampa Rebellion. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• First Police Station Attacked – Chintapalli
• Date – 22 August 1922
• Movement – Rampa Rebellion

The Hyderabad State Congress, formed in 1938, was immediately banned by the Nizam's government. The patriotic song "Veeragandhamu Techhinaramu – Veerulevvaro Telpudi..." was composed during the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–22) to inspire people to participate in the national struggle against British rule. The song became popular among freedom fighters in Andhra and was sung in public meetings, processions and nationalist gatherings. It encouraged sacrifice, patriotism and courage during the early phase of the Gandhian movement. Nationalist songs played a vital role in awakening political consciousness and mobilizing people throughout the freedom struggle. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Movement – Non-Cooperation Movement
• Theme – Patriotism and National Awakening

s:
Match Group – A with Group – B and select the correct answer using the codes given below.
Group – A (Book) Group – B (Author)

a. Japaneeyamu i. Gurajada Appa Rao

b. Mahaprasthanam ii. Sri Sri

c. Kanyasulkam iii. Puchalapalli Sundarayya

d. Veyipadagalu iv. Viswanatha Satyanarayana
v. Sriram Veerabrahmam
x:
Japaneeyamu was written by Sriram Veerabrahmam, reflecting his observations and thoughts on Japan and its society. Mahaprasthanam, the masterpiece of Sri Sri, revolutionized Telugu poetry by introducing progressive ideas and free verse. It remains one of the most influential works in modern Telugu literature. Kanyasulkam, authored by Gurajada Appa Rao, is regarded as the greatest social drama in Telugu literature. It exposed social evils such as child marriage, dowry and exploitation of women through satire and realistic characterization. Veyipadagalu, written by Viswanatha Satyanarayana, is one of the greatest Telugu novels. It portrays the gradual decline of traditional Indian society and is considered a classic of Telugu fiction. Thus, the correct matching is a–v, b–ii, c–i, d– iv, corresponding to Option (4).
Exam Note:
• Mahaprasthanam – Sri Sri
• Kanyasulkam – Gurajada Appa Rao
• Veyipadagalu – Viswanatha Satyanarayana
• Japaneeyamu – Sriram Veerabrahmam
